newsitem.title: CANADA: Agrium sees strong 1997 crop season.
newsitem.headline: Agrium sees strong 1997 crop season.

text.p: Agrium Inc said on Thursday it expected high fertilizer application rates and a strong crop year in 1997 despite current rains and floods in the northern United States and Canadian prairies.

Agrium, which earlier reporter lower first-quarter earnings, said that last autumn's weather-shortened fertilizer application season and low crop nutrient carry-over amounts were expected to result in strong demand for its wholesale products.

"The corporation's enhanced distribution capability in its market areas, a result of the recent Viridian merger, will be a major benefit," Agrium said. "Our retail operations are also expecting a strong spring season."

The company said the process of merging Viridian was complete, making Agrium the largest North American producer and marketer of nitrogen fertilizer and a major producer and marketer of potash and phosphate fertilizers.
During the first quarter, Agrium started construction of 10 new farm centers in Argentina expected to open in the second quarter, bringing its total in the country to 18.
In early April, the company announced it was in talks to form a joint venture with Argentina's YPF SA and Perez SA to develop nitrogen fertilizer production facilities at Bahia Blanca.
